extracted.intended_audience: CS systems and networking researchers — authors and reviewers (especially early-career) interested in learning how to write and evaluate paper reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on creating effective peer reviews for systems/networking conference papers, focusing on review-writing skills and norms rather than selection procedures. Emphasizes learning to review, understanding venue-specific expectations, and using existing resources and PC guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn reviewing as a teachable skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning how to review papers not only (obviously) makes you a better reviewer, but it can also help you as an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat reviewing as a skill to be learned and improved; practice reviewing to become a more effective evaluator and to gain insights that will improve your own writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand reviewer criteria to tailor submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding reviewer criteria helps authors tailor submissions for acceptance — strategic advantage in the submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should learn what reviewers value (evaluation criteria) so they can emphasize those points in their submissions; use knowledge of review criteria to present contributions and evidence clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow venue-specific norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Norms are venue-specific (systems / networking has its own conventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt reviews and papers to the conventions and expectations of the specific conference or community (e.g., typical proof/experiment standards, scope of contributions). Consult conference-specific summaries and past accepted papers to internalize norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on creation of the review (constructive content) rather than only selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The article focuses on 'the creation of a paper review' rather than the paper-selection process for accept/reject decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing a review, prioritize clear, constructive evaluation: identify strengths and weaknesses, explain reasons, suggest fixes, and provide evidence rather than merely voting or flagging accept/reject. Structure reviews to be useful to authors and PCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use established resources and PC guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Feamster directs readers to several established resources: articles explaining the review process and its limitations; guidance on writing effective reviews; conference-specific summaries; Program Committee chair guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn from the literature and official PC guidance: read how-to-review articles, venue summaries, and PC chair notes to align your reviews with best practices and chair expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain empathy: reviewers should remember they were authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should remember they were authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply empathy when reviewing: give actionable feedback, avoid unnecessarily harsh language, and consider how critique will help authors improve. Balancing rigor with respect improves the review process.
